title: A heat-to-stress ratio term remains negative in recent NCEP flux-error changes at 19 tropical sites
abstract: We partition the change in NCEP latent heat flux error at 19 tropical buoy sites between 2010-2019 and February 2023-December 2025. The exact symmetric partition uses the square root of monthly stress-vector magnitude and an effective heat-to-stress ratio. In R1, the error change of -18.82 W/m2 contains a stress term of -5.39 and a ratio term of -13.43 W/m2. In R2, the corresponding terms are -29.13, -9.58 and -19.55 W/m2. Conditional paired block intervals for both ratio terms exclude zero. The ratio terms supply 71% and 67% of the point changes, but their differences from the stress terms are uncertain. Alternate baselines and stricter coverage retain negative ratio terms. The Atlantic carries the largest ratio change. This resolves part of the gap between separate heat-flux and stress checks: a stress-based scaling alone leaves a substantial heat-loss discrepancy. The ratio includes humidity, stability, transfer coefficients and sampling. It is not a pure SST effect or a causal correction. Sparse sites, bulk flux estimates and only three recent years limit the result.

display.caption: Exact partition of the recent NCEP-minus-buoy heat-loss error change. Both stress-scale and heat-to-stress ratio terms are negative. Bars show point estimates; lines show conditional paired bootstrap 95% limits. The terms add exactly, but neither is a causal attribution.
